decisions.mark: explains that the health monitor does NOT invoke its status callback from the monitor thread — it queues events under a mutex and the caller drains them on its own thread
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Events are queued under `event_mutex_`. `process_events()` swaps the queue out and runs callbacks on the engine thread, so callbacks never run on the monitor thread. | WHY: The answer states that events are queued under a mutex and callbacks are run by process_events() on the engine (caller) thread, not the monitor thread. || QUOTE: Events are queued under `event_mutex_`. `process_events()` swaps the queue out and runs callbacks on the engine thread, so callbacks never run on the monitor thread. | WHY: The answer states events are queued under a mutex and callbacks run on the caller's (engine) thread via process_events, not the monitor thread. || QUOTE: Events are queued under `event_mutex_`. `process_events()` swaps the queue out and runs callbacks on the engine thread, so callbacks never run on the monitor thread. | WHY: The answer states that events are queued under a mutex and callbacks are run by process_events() on the engine thread, not the monitor thread.
